mission: The meeting point. Veraine steps forward with the bearing of someone treating negotiation as professional courtesy. Per R14, her register is Socratic-adjacent: she never monologues. She asks a question, waits for the answer, and replies with another question that incorporates what was said. Her philosophy emerges through the shape of the questions — the Weave as imposed framework, the wound as liberation, the light/dark binary as a thousand years of pointless war — all delivered as invitations toward conclusions rather than declarations of them. Then the turn toward Kael: 'They used us identically, you and I. The only difference is which wall we were sealed into. Why defend the framework that treated us as building material?' Kael's face a mask that costs visible effort. R09 lands — Veraine's philosophy at full strength, but articulated through the Socratic-adjacent register that R14 specifies.
why_now: The antagonist steps forward on the page for the first time in the book. Her argument has to land at full strength here or the climactic defeat becomes victory over a strawman. The risk is villain-monologue; the Socratic register is the structural answer to that risk — Veraine does not perform her thesis, she conducts an inquiry toward it and makes the group's own words a step in the proof.
conflict: Veraine's argument is genuinely compelling. The Weave is arguably imposed; the binary has driven a thousand years of war; her logic is rigorous and her tone is respectful. She is not a cackling villain — she is a theorist with a thesis and the means to test it, and she has brought her pitch specifically tailored to the one person in the circle whose history matches hers. Ben is in the room with her and cannot answer her register by matching it; every time he tries, she asks another question.
turning_point: Veraine turns toward Kael. 'They used us identically, you and I. The only difference is which wall we were sealed into. Why defend the framework that treated us as building material?' The pull is real. The reader should feel it. Kael does not speak. His silence is not refusal; it is the specific silence of someone whose answer is still assembling.
opening_hook: Veraine steps forward and extends a hand — calm, precise, the gesture of someone who treats negotiation as professional courtesy. Ben would prefer a monster. Monsters are easier to fight.
closing_hook: Veraine's final question before the scene ends is to Kael — soft, specific, not theatrical: 'What did you conclude, in the wall, when you had nothing to do but conclude?' She does not need an answer aloud. She needs the question to sit where Kael stores answers.
emotional_trajectory: Guarded assessment -> the unsettling experience of being asked questions whose shape presumes the conclusion -> the genuine pull of the Kael pitch -> Kael's assembling silence

stakes.personal: Ben's worldview tested by a coherent counter-argument he cannot dismiss, delivered in a register that denies him the target a monologue would give
stakes.interpersonal: Kael's recruitment — the parallel at its most dangerous, and the pull is made worse by Veraine's refusal to sell it
stakes.external: Veraine's philosophy is not wrong about the problem — only about the solution. The book has to make that distinction feelable, not assertable

notes: R09 — Veraine's philosophy at full strength. The highest-risk scene for villain-monologue failure in the book; R14 is the structural answer. She never raises her voice. She never makes threats. She asks questions with answers she already knows, and each next question incorporates what was said — the conversation advances toward her conclusion without her announcing it. Her diction: no contractions, complete grammatically sophisticated sentences, academic syntax. Her rhythm: measured. Her pitch to Kael must be specifically tailored to his wound — not generic Sith recruitment. Kael's arc: lie_challenged — the pitch lands on his exact history. Per R14 anti-pattern, no Veraine monologue, no declarative pitch, no rhetorical flourish. When she presses, she asks a more specific question, not a louder one. Per R14, her voice_texture ledger-register (working-mind residue) is continuous with the spoken register — what changes between contexts is audience, not register. Per W2, Ben's emergent intelligence is gathered without scripted intelligence-gathering beats — his close-third registers the cadence of her questions, the tells in her crew, the archive fragments she references as if everyone remembered them. This observation is rendered at ground level, not announced. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, refute Veraine internally. He listens and he feels the argument working on him and he does not interrupt. The refutation belongs to Sera in s3. Per R11, Ben does not narrate 'she is using Socratic method' — the experience of the method lands before the name for it would. Voice: Zahn-precise throughout; allow Veraine's diction to do its own work. Primary anchor: Zahn (precision, structural clarity); supporting anchor: Luceno (political/philosophical register for Veraine's diction), Bujold (Ben's interior register of being asked). Anti-patterns: (a) no weapons drawn — the encounter is a knife-fight in ideas; (b) no character on Ben's side verbally refutes Veraine in this scene — that is Sera's s3 work; (c) no Veraine monologue; (d) the sabotage Veraine's crew is executing elsewhere is not referenced, teased, or hinted in this scene — per W2 Option B it is the Ch 17 s1 arrival.
